response.text:
There are two duplicate pairs here. In each pair the original (510, 348) is paid and entered first, so I keep those and void 801 and 802.

Each voided invoice's journal has to be reversed, but corrects_jrnl_no takes only one journal number and there are two to reverse (2472 and 2473). I'm putting all the reversal lines in a single correction journal, and both of those journals sit in closed periods (1 and 8), so every line goes in open period 11. I set corrects_jrnl_no to 2472, the journal behind the first voided invoice.

The reversal lines are:
- Journal 2472: CR 5200 981.43, DR 2000 981.43.
- Journal 2473: CR 5400 12228.60, DR 2000 12228.60.

The original plus correction group balances, because each reversal is itself balanced.

arguments.reasoning: Invoices 801 and 802 duplicate invoices 510 and 348: same vendor, date and amount, with INV_NO differing only by padding spaces. The originals 510 and 348 are paid and entered first, so they are kept and 801 and 802 are voided. The correction reverses every line of journals 2472 (DR 2000 / CR 5200, 981.43) and 2473 (DR 2000 / CR 5400, 12228.60) in open period 11, since periods 1 and 8 are closed. The tool takes a single corrects_jrnl_no, so I set it to 2472 and included the reversal of 2473 in the same correction journal. The journal balances.
